acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Crocodilians family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Bastion Alligator, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Armored-Rotation Champion archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Broad armored alligator with high osteoderms, blunt skull, scarred belly seams, and an extremely powerful tail.
Signature mechanic: Three-Beat Roll: locked side scutes protect two beats and expose the pale belly fault on the second rotation.
battlefieldDuty: Present a scute wall and commit to a fixed-direction death roll that exposes its softer belly at regular intervals.
constructionDimensions: Scute edges and water spray stretch into directional pressure fins while the low opaque body stays heavy and grounded.
Wind pushes a readable wake ahead of lunges and curls along the fixed death-roll direction.
counterplay: Evade away from the tail curve and strike the belly fault during the second roll. Affinity signal: The pressure layer collapses at the jaw hinge, inner curve, or belly during the normal punish window.
forbiddenTreatments: Turbulence that obscures shoreline or rotation direction
identityInvariants: Every form retains a low four-legged crocodilian body, long tail, scuted back, belly fault, sensory pits, and a jaw-driven attack silhouette.
Tier escalation uses snout geometry, scute height, neck mobility, tail mass, scars, and waterline behavior rather than equipment or wings.
Eyes, wake direction, jaw angle, foreclaw grooves, tail curve, and exposed belly keep ambush and rotation counterplay readable.
telegraph: Side scutes lock together and the tail curves strongly against the coming rotation.
